questions.q: Let $M$~and $m$ respectively be the maximum and minimum values of the function $f ( x ) = \tan^{- 1} ( sinx + cosx )$ in  \left[0, \dfrac{π}{2}\right]$. Then the value of $tan ( M - m )$ is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given, the function,& $f ( x ) = \tan^{- 1} ( sinx + cosx )$~in~ \left[0, \dfrac{π}{2}\right]$

$f^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{cosx - sinx}{1 + \left(sinx + cosx\right)2}$

$= \dfrac{cosx - sinx}{1 + sin2x}$

$f^{'}\left(x\right) = 0$

$cosx - sinx = 0$

$tanx = 1$

$x = \dfrac{π}{4}$
Then,~$1 \le sinx + cosx \le \sqrt{2}x \in \left[\dfrac{π}{4}, \tan^{- 1}\sqrt{2}\right]
$M = \tan^{- 1} ( $\sqrt{2} )

$m = \tan^{- 1} ( 1 )$

$M - m = \tan^{- 1} \left(\sqrt{2}\right) - \tan^{- 1} \left(1\right)$

$M - m = \tan^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2} - 1}{1 + \sqrt{2}}\right)

$M - m = \tan^{- 1} ( 3 - $2\sqrt{2} )

$tan ( M - m ) = 3 - $2\sqrt{2}

$

questions.q: Let $f\left(x\right) = \left(x + 3\right)2\left(x - 2\right)3, x \in [ - 4, 4 ]$. If $M$ and $m$ are the maximum and minimum values of $f$, respectively in $[ - 4, 4 ]$, then the value of $M - m$ is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$

Given: $f\left(x\right) = \left(x + 3\right)2 \left($x - 2\right)3$

$⇒ f^{'}\left($x\right) = \left($x + 3\right)2 $\times \left(3\right) \left($x - 2\right)2 + \left($x - 2\right)3\left($2\right)\left($x + 3\right)$

$⇒ f^{'} \left(x\right) = \left(x + 3\right) \left($x - 2\right)2 \left[\left(x + 3\right)\times\left($3\right) + \left($x - 2\right)\left(2\right)\right]$

$⇒ f^{'} \left(x\right) = \left(x + 3\right)\left(x - 2\$right)2\left[$3x + 9 + 2x - 4\right]$

$⇒ f^{'} \left($x\right) = \left(x + 3\right)\left(x - 2\right)2\left(5x + 5\right)$

$⇒ f^{'} \left(x\right) = 5 \left($x + 3\right)\left(x - 2\right)2\left(x + 1\right)$

For critical points, we put $f^{'}\left(x\right) = 0$.

$⇒ 5\left(x + 3\$right)\left($x - 2\$right)2\left($x + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ x = - 3, 2, - 1$

$⇒ $f\left(-$3\right) = $f\left($2\right) = 0$

$⇒ f \left(-$1\right) = {2}^{2} \left(-$3\right)3 = - 108$

Also, $x \in \left[-$4, 4\right]$

$⇒ f ( - 4 ) = - 216$

$⇒ f ( 4 ) = 49 $\times$8 = 392$

$⇒ M = 392, m = - 216$

$⇒ M - m = 392 + 216$

$⇒ M - m = 608

An isosceles triangle with base equal to $2r$.

$h = rsin\theta + r$

base $= BC = 2rcos\theta$

$\theta \in \left[$0, $\dfrac{π}{2}\right)

Area of \Delta$ABC = $\dfrac{1}{2} \left($BC\right) . h$

\Delta = $\dfrac{1}{2}\llleft(2rcos\theta\right) . \l$lleft(rsin\theta +$r\right)$

$= r^{2} $\l$left(cos\theta\right) . \left(1 + sin\theta\right)$

\dfrac{d\Delta}{d\theta} =r^{2}\l$left[cos\theta\dfrac{d}{d\theta} \left($1 + $sin\theta\right) +\left(1 + sin\theta\$right)\dfrac{d}{d\theta}\lleft($cos\theta\right)\right]

$\dfrac{d\Delta}{d\theta} =r^{2} \left[$cos$\theta\left(0 + cos\theta\right) + \left(1 + sin\theta\right)\left(- sin\theta\right)\right]$

\dfrac{d\Delta}{d\theta} =$r^{2} \left[\cos^{2}\theta -$sin$\theta - \sin^{2}\theta\right]

$\dfrac{d\Delta}{d\theta} =r^{2} \left[1 - \sin^{2}\theta - sin\theta - \sin^{2}\theta\right]$

$= r^{2} \left[1 - sin\theta --2\sin^{2}\theta\right]

$= r^{2} \left[-2\sin^{2}\theta -sin\theta +$1\right]$

$= r^{2} \left[-$2\sin^{2}$\theta -$2sin$\theta +$sin$\theta +$1\right]$

$= r^{2} \left[- 2sin\theta \lleft(sin\theta +1\right) + $1\l$left(sin\theta +$1\right)\right]$

$⇒ $\theta = \dfrac{π}{6}

$⇒$~\Deltais maximum where \theta = \dfrac{π}{6}

${Δ}_\max = $\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{4}$r^{2} =$ area of equilateral \Deltawith~$BC = $\sqrt{3}$r$.

questions.q: Let the function $f ( x ) = 2x^{3} + ( 2p - 7 ) x^{2} + 3 ( 2p - 9 ) x - 6$~have a maxima for some value of $x < 0$~and a minima for some value of $x > 0$. Then, the set of all values of $p$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given,$f ( x ) = 2x^{3} + ( 2p - 7 ) x^{2} + 3 ( 2p - 9 ) x - 6$

On taking differentiation w.r.t~$x$, we get

$f^{'} ( x ) = 6x^{2} + 2 ( 2p - 7 ) x + 3 ( 2p - 9 )$

$⇒ f^{'} ( 0 ) = 6 ( 0{)}^{2} + 2 ( 2p - 7 ) ( 0 ) + 3 ( 2p - 9 )$

$⇒ f^{'} ( 0 ) = 3 ( 2p - 9 )$

Here, given that for~$x < 0$~the function has maxima and for~$x > 0$~the function has minima so the function is decreasing function about~$x = 0$,

Hence~$f^{'} ( 0 ) < 0$

So,~$3 ( 2p - 9 ) < 0$

$⇒ p < \dfrac{9}{2}$

Therefore,~$p \in \left(- \infty , \dfrac{9}{2}\right)$

$

questions.q: Let $f  \left(x\right)$ be a polynomial of degree $5$ such that $x = \pm1$ are its critical points. If $\lim_{x \to 0}\left(2 + $\dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{x3}\right) =$4, then which one of the following is not true?$
options: $f\left(1\right) - 4f\left(- 1\right) = 4$ . $x = 1$ is a point of maximum and $x = - 1$
$x = 1$is a point of local minimum and~$x = - 1$& is a point of local maximum
$x = 1$~is a point of local maxima of $f$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$f\left(x\right) = ax^{5} + bx^{4} + cx^{3}$

Consider,~$\lim_{x \to 0} ⁡ \left(2 + \dfrac{ax^{5} + bx^{4} + cx^{3}}{x3}\right) = 4$

$⇒ 2 + c = 4$

$⇒ c = 2$

Differentiating~$f \left(x\right)$~with respect to~$x$

$f^{'} \left(x\right) = 5ax^{4} + 4bx^{3} + 6x^{2}$

$= x^{2}\left(5ax^{2} + 4bx + 6\right)$

Critical points of the function are given as~$\pm1$.

$f^{'}\left(1\right) = 0 ⇒ 5a + 4b + 6 = 0$

$f^{'}\left(-1\right) = 0 ⇒ 5a - 4b + 6 = 0$
Solving both we get,~$b = 0$,~$a = - \dfrac{6}{5}$
So,~$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{- 6}{5}x^{5} + 2x^{3}$
And~$f^{'} \left(x\right) = - 6x^{4} + 6x^{2}$

$= - 6x^{2}\left(x + 1\right)\left(x - 1\right)$

Hence, local minima at $x = - 1$~and local maxima~at $x = 1.

$

questions.q: If& ${a}_{α}$~is the greatest term in the sequence~${a}_{n} = \dfrac{n3}{n^{4} + 147}, n = 1, 2, 3 . . . . ,$~then~$\alpha$~is equal to~______

Let,

We know that, for increasing function~\dfrac{dy}{dx}$> 0$

So, differentiating the given function~$f\left(x\right) = $\dfrac{x3}{x^{4} + 147}~we get,

$∵ f\left(5\right) > f\left(4\right)$

$⇒ \alpha =5

questions.q: A wire of length $36m$ is cut into two pieces, one of the pieces is bent to form a square and the other is bent to form a circle. If the sum of the areas of the two figures is minimum, and the circumference of the circle is $k$ (meter), then \left(\dfrac{4}{π} + 1\right)k$ is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Let the side of square be $x$~and radius of circle be $y$.

$4x + 2\piy = 36$~(given)

Area,~$A = x^{2} + \piy^{2}$

$⇒ A = x^{2} + \pi\left(\dfrac{36 - 4x}{2\pi}\right)2$

$⇒ ⇒ A = x^{2} + \dfrac{1}{π} \left(18 - 2x\right)2$

$⇒ $\dfrac{dA}{dx} =$2x + $\dfrac{2}{π}\left($18 - 2x\$right)\left(-$2\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{dA}{dx} = \dfrac{2\pix + ( 36 - 4x ) ( - 2 )}{π}$

For critical points

$\dfrac{dA}{dx} =0$

$⇒ 2\pix - 72 + 8x = 0$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{36}{\pi + 4}$

Now,

$\dfrac{d^{2}A}{dx^{2}} = \left(2 + $\dfrac{8}{π}\right)

$⇒ $\dfrac{d^{2}A}{dx^{2}}$> 0$

Hence, area is minimized.

$y = $\dfrac{18}{\pi + 4}
$K$~[circumference of circle)$= 2\piy ⇒ k = $\dfrac{36\pi}{( \pi + 4 )}

questions.q: Let $f  \left(x\right)$~be a cubic polynomial with $f \left(1\right) = - 10, f  \left(-1\right) = 6,$~and has a local minima at $x = 1,$~and $f^{'}\left(x\right)$ has a local minima at $x = - 1 .$~Then $f  \left($3\right)$ is equal to& <u>& & & & & & </u> .$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let,& $f\left(x\right) = ax^{3} + bx^{2} + cx + d$

Diff w. r. t.~ '$x$'

$f^{'}\left(x\right) = 3ax^{2} + 2bx + c$

Again diff. w. r. t.~ '$x$'

$f^{"}\left(x\right) = 6ax + 2b$

$f^{"}\left(- 1\right) = 0$

$- 6a + 2b = 0$

$b = 3a$

$f ' \left(1\right) = 0$

$3a + 6a + c = 0$

$c = - 9a$

$f \left(1\right) = - 10$~

$- 5a + d = - 10 \ldots \left(i\right)$

$f ( - 1 ) = 6$~

$11a + d = 6 \ldots \left(ii\right)$

From equations~ \left(i\right) - \left(ii\right)$

We get~$a = 1, d = - 5, b = 3, c = - 9$

Then,~$f\left(x\right) = x^{3} + 3x^{2} - 9x - 5$

Hence, $f\left(3\right) = 27 + 27 - 27 - 5$

$f\left(3\right) = 22$

$

questions.q: Let $P ( x )$ be a real polynomial of degree $3$~which vanishes at $x = - 3$.~Let $P ( x )$ have local minima~at $x = 1$, local maxima at $x = - 1$~and~${∫}_{- 1}^{1}P\left(x\right)dx = 18$, then the sum of all the~coefficients of the polynomial $P ( x )$ is equal to ___ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let& $P^{'} ( x ) = a ( x - 1 ) ( x + 1 ) = a \left(x^{2} - 1\right)$

$P\left(x\right) = a ∫ \left(x^{2} - 1\right)dx + c$

$= a\left(\dfrac{x3}{3} -x\right) + c$

Now $P ( - 3 ) = 0$

$⇒ a\left(- \dfrac{27}{3} +3\right) + c = 0$

$⇒ - 6a + c = 0 \ldots ( 1 )$

Now ${∫}_{- 1}^{1} \left(a \left(\dfrac{x3}{3} -x\right) + c\right)dx = 18$

$= 2c = 18 ⇒ c = 9 . . . \left(2\right)$

~From~$( 1 ) \text{ and } ( 2 )$~$⇒ - 6a + 9 = 0 ⇒ a = \dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒ P\left(x\right) = \dfrac{3}{2}\left(\dfrac{x3}{3} -x\right) + 9$

Then, the Sum of coefficient$= \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{3}{2} +9$

$= 8$
